page: Amazon Web Services c7a.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a single dedicated x86_64 vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. This single physical core operates without hyperthreading and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 4 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the dedicated AMD EPYC core delivers strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 3031.18 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the top 25% of tested servers. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core performance is limited, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3031.18 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1941.0, both falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory performance shows average write bandwidth for large blocks at 28.35 GB/sec, but read-only bandwidth is weak to poor, registering 34.27 GB/sec for large blocks and 147.72 GB/sec for cached small blocks. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression achieve average performance tiers at 29.24 GB/sec and 13.53 GB/sec respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the c7a.medium is its single-core limitation, which restricts its utility for highly parallelized tasks, as evidenced by poor scores in multi-threaded compiling, ray tracing, and database operations. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated, high-frequency single-core execution without the overhead of multi-threading. This instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, small-scale single-threaded web serving, or low-intensity LLM text generation using small models.
